workTitle: Symphony No. 41 in C major, K. 551

clues.label: A musical characteristic
clues.text: The finale juggles five different themes in invertible counterpoint — and in the last bars he stacks all five on top of each other.

clues.label: A historical event connected to the composer
clues.text: In 1781 he walked out on his boss, an archbishop, and tried to make it as a freelancer in the imperial capital. Bold move. Also a good way to go broke.

clues.label: Places the composer lived and worked
clues.text: Born in a prince-archbishop's town on the Salzach. Last ten years in the imperial capital; dead there in 1791, age thirty-five. This piece is from those last years.

clues.label: A biographical detail
clues.text: His father hauled him around Europe as a kid, showing him off at courts before he was even ten.

clues.label: An anecdote
clues.text: He was the child genius. He died at thirty-five leaving a Requiem unfinished — a mysterious patron, a grave outside the city walls, the whole legend. And that little night-music serenade they play at every wedding? Also him.

explanation.summary: A Salzburg prodigy who went freelance in Vienna, and a finale that stacks five themes at once: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, writing in Austria in 1788.

points.text: Five themes stacked in invertible counterpoint at the end — that's the "Jupiter" Symphony, K. 551.
Walking out on Archbishop Colloredo in 1781 is the move from Salzburg to Vienna.
The town on the Salzach is Salzburg — his birthplace, not the answer here. The last three symphonies were written in Vienna in the summer of 1788.
Those childhood tours, run by his father Leopold, are on a scale nobody else matches.
The Requiem, the common grave, and Eine kleine Nachtmusik. The anonymous commission came from Count Franz von Walsegg. Mozart died in Vienna in December 1791.
